title: Binomials of a transcendental parameter are irreducible
statement: Let $F\subseteq E$ be fields [def-pc-field-extension], let $r\geq1$, and let $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in E$ be algebraically independent over $F$, meaning that evaluation of a polynomial in these $r$ variables is zero only for the zero polynomial [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis]. Let $K=F(t_1,\ldots,t_r)\subseteq E$ be the smallest subfield containing $F$ and these elements. For every integer $m\geq1$, the polynomial $X^m-t_1\in K[X]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] is irreducible: it is a nonzero nonunit, and in any factorization in $K[X]$ one factor is a unit. No restriction on the characteristic of $F$ or on divisibility of $m$ by that characteristic is imposed.

source.place: Polynomial.irreducible_of_eisenstein_criterion, lines 175--180, applied over F(t_2,...,t_r)[t_1] at (t_1), followed by Polynomial.Monic.irreducible_iff_irreducible_map_fraction_map, Mathlib/RingTheory/Polynomial/GaussLemma.lean:149--150. proof.text:
Put $B=F[t_2,\ldots,t_r]\subset E$ and $G=F(t_2,\ldots,t_r)$, taking both equal to $F$ if $r=1$. The fractions $b/c$ with $b,c\in B$, $c
e0$, form a subfield of $E$ containing $F,t_2,\ldots,t_r$, and every such fraction belongs to $G$; hence they are exactly $G$. If $\sum_{i=0}^d g_it_1^i=0$ with $g_i\in G$, write $g_i=b_i/c_i$ and multiply by $c=\prod_i c_i
e0$. For each $i$, represent $b_i\prod_{j
e i}c_j\in B$ by a polynomial $q_i$ in the last $r-1$ variables over $F$. The polynomial $\sum_i q_i(Y_2,\ldots,Y_r)Y_1^i$ evaluates to zero at the given family; algebraic independence [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis] makes it the zero polynomial. Its coefficients $q_i$ are therefore zero, so $cg_i=0$ and $g_i=0$. Thus evaluation $G[T]	o E$, $T\mapsto t_1$, is injective.

source.place: elementary parameter-ring argument for X^m-t_1 over F(t_2,...,t_r)[t_1]

proof.text: Write $A=G[T]$ and identify it with $G[t_1]\subset E$ by Step 1. Fractions of elements of $G[t_1]$ form a subfield containing $F,t_1,\ldots,t_r$, so contain $K$; conversely $K$ contains all these fractions. Thus $K$ is a fraction field of $A$ via $j:A\to K$, $T\mapsto t_1$: $j$ is an injective unital ring map and every element of $K$ is $j(a)/j(b)$ with $a,b\in A$, $b\ne0$.

source.place: elementary parameter-ring argument for X^m-t_1 over F(t_2,...,t_r)[t_1]

proof.text: For $m\ge1$ set $f=X^m-T\in A[X]$; its leading coefficient is $1$, so it is monic of degree $m$. Put $C=G[X]$. Regrouping a finite sum $\sum_{i,j}a_{ij}T^iX^j$ by powers of $T$ identifies $A[X]=G[T][X]$ with $C[T]$ as rings, since in both rings the product is the same convolution of the coefficient arrays $(a_{ij})$. In $C[T]$ we have $f=(-1)T+X^m$, of $T$-degree $1$ with $T$-coefficient $-1$. The ring $C$ is a domain, since the product of the leading coefficients of two nonzero polynomials over the field $G$ is nonzero; hence $T$-degrees add under products in $C[T]$. So $f\ne0$, and $f$ is not a unit, because $fg=1$ would force $1+\deg_Tg=0$. Let $f=gh$ in $C[T]$. Then $\deg_Tg+\deg_Th=1$, so one factor, say $g$, has $T$-degree $0$, i.e. $g=c\in C$. Write $h=h_1T+h_0$ with $h_0,h_1\in C$; the $T$-coefficient gives $ch_1=-1$, so $c$ is a unit of $C$ and hence of $C[T]$. Thus $f$ is irreducible in $A[X]$. Nothing here depends on the characteristic of $G$.

source.place: degree count in T after regrouping G[T][X]=G[X][T] (replaces the earlier Eisenstein application).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-monic-polynomial-fraction-field-irreducibility] to the field $G$, the ring $A=G[T]$, its fraction field $K$ verified in Step 2, and the monic polynomial $f$ of Step 3, irreducible in $A[X]$. Its image has coefficient $1$ at degree $m$, coefficient $-t_1$ at degree $0$, and zero elsewhere, so is exactly $X^m-t_1$. The forward implication of the cited equivalence gives its irreducibility in $K[X]$, with all the clauses specified in the statement. Neither Step 3 nor the cited equivalence requires separability or an exponent invertible in $F$.
